seo.title: Portland Metro Roofing Contractor
seo.description: Residential and commercial roofing in {{city}}, Oregon. Roof installation, repairs, maintenance and gutter systems from a licensed, bonded and insured contractor.

hero.lead: Installation, repairs, maintenance and gutter systems across {{serviceArea}}, from a crew small enough that the person who quotes your job is the person on your roof.

tiles.title: Residential
tiles.body: Roof replacement, leak repairs and seasonal maintenance for homes across {{serviceArea}}, plus the gutters and custom flashing that keep water moving off the roof and away from the house.

image.alt: Aerial view of a brick house with a new architectural shingle roof

tiles.title: Commercial
tiles.body: Single-ply and low-slope systems for shops, warehouses and light-industrial buildings, installed to spec and detailed properly at every curb, drain and penetration.

image.alt: Crew rolling out and detailing white membrane on a low-slope commercial roof

tiles.title: Multi-unit
tiles.body: Apartments, condos and townhome rows: replacement, repair and scheduled maintenance, planned building by building around the people living underneath.

image.alt: Aerial view of rows of townhomes with gray shingle roofs

materials.title: Roofing materials for every roof and budget
materials.lead: Architectural and designer shingle for steep roofs, membrane for flat ones. We'll recommend the one that suits the pitch, the budget and an Oregon winter, and tell you why.

items.title: Architectural shingle
items.body: Thicker, laminated shingle with a dimensional profile that reads like shake. Heavy and wind-rated, in a wide range of colors. The standard choice on most house re-roofs.

items.title: Designer shingle
items.body: Premium, extra-thick shingle cut to look like slate or hand-split shake. Deeper shadow lines and the heaviest weight of any asphalt shingle, for a roof that shows from the street.

items.title: Single-ply membrane (TPO / PVC)
items.body: Heat-welded membrane for flat and low-slope roofs, residential or commercial. Seams are fused into one continuous, watertight sheet.
